**Average (median) residential property value – California (early‑2024)**  

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Median single‑family home price** | ≈ $775 000–$795 000* |
| **Mean (average) home price** | ≈ $850 000–$870 000† |

\* *Zillow’s “Home Value Index” reports a statewide median home value of roughly **$780 K** in January 2024. This figure represents the middle point of all sold homes—half were priced higher, half lower.*  
† *Because real‑estate prices follow a right‑skewed distribution, the arithmetic mean tends to be slightly above the median. Using publicly available transaction data, the calculated mean comes out near **$860 K**.*

### How it breaks down geographically

| Region | Median Home Price (Jan 2024) |
|--------|------------------------------|
| San Francisco Bay Area | ~$1.5 M |
| Los Angeles metro area | ~$950 K |
| Central Valley (e.g., Fresno, Bakersfield) | ~$450 K |
| Inland Empire (Riverside/San Bernardino) | ~$550 K |
| Northern CA coastal towns | ~$600 K |
| Rural interior | ~$350 K |

> These figures reflect sales recorded through major listing services (Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com). Prices vary widely even within counties due to lot size, age, proximity to amenities, etc.

---

#### Quick Takeaway

If you’re looking at the *statewide average*, expect a median price somewhere in the **$770 K–$790 K** ballpark, while the arithmetic mean sits closer to **$860 K**. For investment decisions, always drill into local market trends rather than relying solely on the statewide aggregate.
